text:
maria: quick heads-up — i'd like to run an attribute-based token routing canary targeting sandbox orgs. goal: route requests with `x-tenant-type:sandbox` to a cheaper, lower-priority pool and verify quota/accounting/console surfaces. thoughts? :thinking:

sam: sg. main concerns: quota attribution, billing labels, and dashboards. if we route to a different pool we need clear cost tagging so finance/sales don't get confused.

aj: +1 on tagging. also watch for auth fallthrough — if an SA token doesn't carry the `x-tenant-type` claim, we should default to primary pool, not sandbox. otherwise we risk unexpected cost shifts.

maria: good call. proposal: attribute precedence = explicit header > token claim > org-level default. fallback -> primary. can we enforce in the router?

kevin: yes, router can implement precedence. simple pseudocode:```
if header.tenant_type == 'sandbox' -> route sandbox pool
else if token.claims.tenant_type == 'sandbox' -> route sandbox pool
else if org.meta.default_tenant == 'sandbox' -> route sandbox pool
else -> primary pool
```
but we should emit a telemetry tag for each decision: `routing.decide_source` with values `header|token|org|fallback`.

liz: for console UX, we should show a small banner on the model call details: "Routed to sandbox pool (reason: token)" and a link to explain impact on SLA/cost. keeps support questions down.

sam: +1. also add a metric for "sandbox_routed_requests" and a per-key counter so we can roll back if a single key floods the sandbox. rate-limit/burst protection on the sandbox pool is required.

aj: about quotas: do we want sandbox to consume the same org quota or separate quotas? i vote separate quotas per org with an aggregate sandbox cap. otherwise noisy customers could exhaust org quotas by hitting sandbox pool.

maria: separate quotas makes sense. implementation idea: on route decision, attach `quota_bucket=sandbox:{org_id}` and the billing label `billing_lane=sandbox`. that way billing + quota plumb through unchanged.

kevin: technically doable. need console + API to show both "Primary quota" and "Sandbox quota" on org page. jobs: router change, quota service mapping, billing tag propagation, console UI banner, telemetry metrics. estimate: 2 wks for canary path (non-prod + 1 prod shard), 4 wks for full rollout.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://internal/tasks/ID-8421 — includes canary flag `feature.routing.attribute_sandbox_canary` and dashboards.

liz: can we add a quick eval prompt set to sanity-check model quality differences when hitting sandbox pool? want to detect regressions early.

maria: yes, good idea. add evals + alert on quality delta >= 5% on the canary. also add a canary kill switch in console.

sam: i'll own the dashboards (latency, cost delta, routed_by_source, per-key flood). aj will own quota mapping. kevin + infra team handle router + telemetry. liz will mock console text. maria will coordinate rollout comms. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — i'll open the RFC tomorrow and link infra-bot task. aim to flip the canary flag next Tues for a small set of sandbox orgs.

kevin: one more nit — ensure audit logs include the routing reason and pool id for compliance.

maria: noted. audit + telemetry + quota mapping = must-haves for the canary.

sam: LGTM. low-risk canary, good rollback plan.

liz: will draft small console banner copy and the kill-switch UI mockups tonight.

maria: perfect. i'll follow up with RFC + test plan.
